paper.title: RippleGUItester: Change-Aware Exploratory Testing
paper.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Software Engineering 3, ISSTA, Article ISSTA149, October 2026
paper.page_convention: All page references are printed ISSTA149:1–22 in the final author PDF; PDF #page is the same 1-based index.
version_differences: Final Table 1: 117 Bug#, 146 TP, 173 FP, precision 45.8%; arXiv v1: 119 Bug#, 148 TP, 171 FP, precision 46.4%. JabRef changes from 17 unique/19 TP/21 FP to 15 unique/17 TP/23 FP.
Final reporting status: 26 reports, 18 fixed, 3 confirmed, 5 intended. arXiv v1: 16 fixed, 2 confirmed, 6 under discussion, 2 intended.

Final Firefox unique TP comparison removes one pre-existing bug: 41 unique introduced TP, 13 overlapping known ground truth, 28 outside it. arXiv v1 had 42 unique TP, 13 overlap, 29 outside it. Both have only 13/46 known-bug recall.

brief.skill: deep-research; narrow close-reading perspective assigned by parent; no subagents spawned
rq: What actually guides test generation and exploration, and which steps are programmatic versus LLM-driven?
What does the final evaluation establish about effectiveness, precision, recall, costs, and individual components?
Which mechanisms and boundaries transfer to source-bound, execution-guided validation augmentation for coding-agent issue resolution?
perspectives: Method reconstruction from the final paper
Transfer to the existing source-bound distinction design
brief.no_execution: Only public source/papers/issue metadata were read. No provider calls, benchmark runs, implementation edits, or issue messages were performed.

artifacts.final_paper_repository_citation: Final PDF p.20 Data Availability; reference [33] p.21 has DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21671184.
artifacts.comparison: All prompt files and executor.py/generation_tool.py/enhancement_tool.py/constructor.py/commit.py are identical between the downloaded old and final repositories. Differences in generator.py/detector.py are output/comment changes; main execution configuration retains the same models and mechanisms. Final repository adds artifact setup, CLI, and metric scripts.

central_characterization.conclusion: Change-guided, scenario-level LLM generation followed by an adaptive GUI executor and an intent-aware differential detector. It is a useful end-to-end testing design, but does not implement source-level dependency propagation or execution-guided search for new scenarios.
central_characterization.novelty_calibration: Do not dismiss it because LLMs, retrieval, differential testing, or GUI automation already exist. Its contribution is a change-aware system composition aimed at indirect end-user effects, with actual externally reported findings. The study does not isolate which component causes the gain.

faithful_algorithm.operation: Collect PR/linked issue summary and description, commit message, modified paths, and patch hunks. For each deleted/modified old line, obtain the last modifying commit using blame/annotate; retrieve its PR/issues and rank preceding change intents by number of overlapping lines (creation time breaks ties in code).
faithful_algorithm.llm_scope: The traceability and counting are algorithmic. Semantic interpretation of impacts is delegated to the generator LLM.
faithful_algorithm.limits: Added-only lines cannot contribute preceding intents through this old-line mechanism. Blame overlap establishes historical association, not data/control dependence, reachability, or causal impact.

faithful_algorithm.operation: GPT-5.2 interprets the current intent, concrete diff, and preceding intents; emits change_intent_explanation, code_changes_explanation, impact_analysis, and end-user scenarios. Scenario steps are actions, with optional textual oracles stored separately.
faithful_algorithm.llm_scope: The LLM performs the actual change-impact analysis and identifies sensitive/high-risk workflows. There is no call graph, dataflow engine, symbolic execution, or source-level execution feedback in this stage.
faithful_algorithm.limits: Default final run configuration has with_file_content=False and with_cochange_file_content=False; code hunks rather than whole-repository semantic analysis form the main code context. Initial prompt limits output to 5 scenarios, preferably fewer.

faithful_algorithm.operation: LLM identifies missing alternative entry points/triggers, generates targeted queries, calls hosted file_search over application-specific historical report text, and integrates retrieved event sequences into independent scenarios. When a scenario would become too complex, it may create another scenario.
faithful_algorithm.llm_scope: The LLM decides queries, relevance and enrichment; retrieval returns text. This is not a formal program path search or a guarantee of execution diversity.
faithful_algorithm.limits: Final prompt limit 7 scenarios. The actual SKB is filtered historical text in vector stores, not an explicit task/state knowledge graph; more comprehensive graphs appear as future work.

faithful_algorithm.operation: GPT-5.2 identifies data requirements, checks candidate examples against inferred constraints, fills concrete examples, and adds boundary/equivalence/valid-invalid/contrasting-outcome variations. It may split scenarios for simplicity.
faithful_algorithm.llm_scope: Data validity and representativeness are reasoned about by the LLM before execution, not proven by a constraint solver. The default data-enhancer call uses no retrieval tools.
faithful_algorithm.limits: Scenario cap remains 7. No coverage metric, mutation distance, or runtime distinction measure ranks scenarios.

faithful_algorithm.operation: In a fresh Docker environment, Claude Opus 4.5 sees the scenario action descriptions, current screenshot, and prior action memory. It selects the next step, resolves preconditions, emits one or more structured coordinate actions, calls the execution tool, receives the resulting screenshot, and repeats.
faithful_algorithm.llm_scope: This is a genuine observation-action loop. The prompt asks it to verify earlier steps, revise failed/repeated actions and adjust coordinates. Algorithmic code implements click, right_click, long_click, double_click, triple_click, input, scroll, drag, move, keypress and wait through GUI utilities.
faithful_algorithm.limits: Budget 20 LLM interactions/35 UI instructions per scenario. Initial expected-outcome oracles are removed from executor input. Default memory is extracted prior tool calls plus current screenshot, rather than retaining historical images. Batched instructions execute without an intervening LLM decision, although screenshots are captured after actions.

faithful_algorithm.operation: Launch pre-change build in a fresh environment and replay exactly the post-change action sequence/coordinates, capturing screenshots. Default wait 3s; Godot replay wait 9s.
faithful_algorithm.llm_scope: Replay itself is algorithmic and nonadaptive in the evaluated/default configuration.
faithful_algorithm.limits: Identical coordinates need not target corresponding semantic widgets after intended layout changes. The paper attributes 11 false positives to this replay mismatch and proposes adaptive replay as future work.

faithful_algorithm.stage: 7. Detect visual differences and classify intent
faithful_algorithm.operation: Compare corresponding screenshots using pixel absdiff, grayscale threshold 30, dilation, connected regions/bounding boxes; annotate both images. For frames with nonempty diff regions, GPT-5.2 receives prior detector dialogue, change-intent summary/explanation, scenario, executed operation, diff boxes and screenshots, and classifies intended differences versus potential bugs.
faithful_algorithm.llm_scope: Pixel differencing is algorithmic; semantic difference interpretation, intendedness, impact and textual bug-report expected/actual behavior are LLM judgments.
faithful_algorithm.limits: Code uses dilation kernel 5x5 for 2 iterations, masks the desktop top bar by 25 pixels, and does not invoke detection on visually identical pairs. No source event observation, assertion execution or independently enforced contract proof is used by this detector.

faithful_algorithm.operation: GPT-5.2 processes report text to remove duplicate root causes, screenshot-timing artifacts and nondeterministic GUI differences. Final report text has summary, reproduction steps, expected and actual behavior.
faithful_algorithm.llm_scope: The public postprocessor reads reports, not a new confirmatory execution or screenshots. It applies classification/heuristics rather than rerunning to establish nondeterminism.
faithful_algorithm.limits: It can leave residual duplicates and false positives. Labeling code consults post_processor.json keep flags before human TP/FP labeling, so Table 1 is not the unfiltered detector-output precision.

present: GUI screenshot/action-memory feedback to next post-change UI action
Dialogue context retained across detector frames
Historical text retrieval conditions event enrichment
absent_in_default_pipeline: No execution outcome fed back to regenerate/enrich scenarios
No coverage-guided or source-fact-guided input mutation loop
No symbolic propagation of change through callers or dataflow
No published search objective or quantified semantic distance
feedback_boundary.qualification: The absence of these mechanisms does not imply that the GUI executor is open-loop. Its execution loop is adaptive; scenario generation is a staged pre-execution process.

skb.construction: Rule filtering removes empty/log-heavy/intermittent reports; GPT-5 Nano classifies whether the description contains any end-user GUI interaction scenario. Retained reports form the SKB and are uploaded as text to hosted vector stores. Paper states overlapping fixed-token chunks with keyword and semantic retrieval.
skb.implementation_detail: Code calls vector_stores.create and vector_stores.files.create without explicit chunk size, overlap, top-k or embedding parameter. Do not invent exact retrieval settings from API defaults; the paper gives the embedding model but no numeric chunk-size parameters.

leakage_caveat.paper_claim: §4.1.3 p.12: only entries created prior to the tested PR creation time are eligible.
leakage_caveat.observed_code: Both inspected repositories' generator.py L103–134 select latest dated vector store <= bug.closed_time. The preparation scripts bucket historical reports by creation_time, but target boundaries use closed_time; GitHub object code maps closed_time from closed_at.
leakage_caveat.conclusion: A verified paper/code temporal-policy discrepancy, not a demonstrated contaminating retrieval. We did not audit actual stored entries/retrieval logs. Do not claim proven benchmark leakage.

models.role: Initial generation, event enrichment, data enrichment

models.settings: max_tokens=12800 in wrapper; no explicit extended-thinking configuration

models.code_note: Hosted vector-store setup does not pin this as an explicit create argument.

models.role: Suitability filtering of candidate GitHub PRs
models.paper: PR filtering mentioned; selector model not separately detailed

model_scope_note: Published experiments use these model families; source wrappers also contain other model constants and defaults (e.g. Sonnet/Haiku/GPT-5), but they are not evidence of evaluated variants or ablation. Executed config passes Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.2 explicitly. Date-pinned inference model snapshots are not given; aliases are used.

evaluation.provenance: Final paper §§4.1–4.5 pp.12–17; primary evidence supplemented by reading final artifact metric/labeling scripts. Metrics were not rerun.

sampling.Firefox: 30 randomly selected merged PRs, each known to introduce >=1 bug. Thus this is a deliberately positive regression-recall sample.
sampling.others: 50 recent PRs for Zettlr, 50 Godot and an expanded 80 JabRef, all before Jan 2026; after suitability/nonfunctional filtering retained 38,25,18.
sampling.selection_caveat: Selector prompt requires simple deterministic easy-to-reproduce preconditions and excludes complex setup, external dependencies and non-trivial data preparation; Ubuntu GUI scope only. This further limits extrapolation to arbitrary repository issue-resolution tasks.

metric_interpretation: Precision is report-level TP/(TP+FP)=146/319=45.8%, with residual duplicates included.
Bug# is a separate deduplicated author-labeled discovery count; for Firefox it subtracts known-ground-truth hits, not all pre-existing bugs.

§4.3 p.14 explicitly says TP includes a small number of bugs already present before the tested change. Official Table 1 script counts is_true_positive irrespective of is_introduced and explicitly performs no special handling for pre-existing bugs.

Firefox Table 1 Bug# = 42 deduplicated TP - 13 known-ground-truth hits = 29, retaining one pre-existing bug. Recall analysis separately removes that pre-existing bug to obtain 41 introduced unique TP.
Therefore do not describe all 146 TP reports or all 117 Bug# as independently confirmed newly introduced regressions.
Human labeling is one annotator reviewing all detected bugs twice (§5 p.18), not independent multi-rater adjudication.

recall.exclusions: 6 insufficiently GUI-described log/stack-trace bugs + 2 duplicate-counted bugs
recall.interpretation: The 41 (or arXiv's 42) unique true positives are not the recall numerator. The 28 outside ground truth have no exhaustively known denominator.
recall.relevant_example: PR fixing Firefox Issue1592682 introduced Issue1725969. Generated tests separately exercise sorting and new-login creation but miss new-login creation while Username sort is active. The combination is missing despite the individual features being tested.
recall.typo_note: The final PDF prints 'Strict trigger steps (5/15)' although the surrounding decomposition is 15 + 5 = 20 generation misses; use absolute counts rather than copying that denominator.

false_positives.term_caution: 173/319 is the false discovery proportion among reported detections, not a classical false positive rate FP/(FP+TN); no TN denominator is supplied.

ablations_and_baselines.observed: No baseline comparison, component ablation or multi-model comparison is reported in the full final paper. The four RQs cover discovery, precision, known-bug recall and overhead.
ablations_and_baselines.supported: End-to-end feasibility and real maintainer-facing findings under the reported settings.
ablations_and_baselines.unsupported: An isolated causal gain from SKB, preceding intents, data enrichment or pixel annotation; superiority to an equal-budget direct prompting baseline; universal upper-bound performance; improved coding-agent issue-resolution rate.

maintainer_evidence.paper_snapshot: 26 submitted latest-version reports: 18 fixed, 3 confirmed, 5 intended (final abstract/§4.2 p.13). Phrase this as the paper's reporting status, not a fresh aggregate or 26 confirmed bugs.
maintainer_evidence.inspection_scope: Read metadata for all 23 linked GitHub issues and 19 nonempty comment threads on 2026-10-16. A closed/completed GitHub issue alone does not establish a fix. No new aggregate status count inferred.

positive_example.symptom: HTTP /libraries/demo returned 500 HTML rather than demo JSON after the server refactoring.
positive_example.evidence: Issue is closed with linked PR 14810; project bot says it was fixed and directs to that PR.

oracle_boundary_examples.finding: Maintainers reject count equality across builds as a general requirement and ask which concrete characters are counted incorrectly. This is direct evidence that differential change alone is not a contract violation.
Maintainer says the preceding bracket should remain outside the link, consistent with CommonMark/Pandoc, and closes as not a bug.
Maintainer says whitespace collapsing is appropriate and not a bug.
The apparent literal tabstop marker is an intentional placeholder for an empty tabstop; maintainer says behavior is intended.
Maintainer closes as outdated translations, not a functional code bug. The paper itself explains the translation cause; keep this distinct from a confirmed semantic code regression.

maintainer_evidence.interpretation: These boundary cases qualify the oracle and reporting counts, while the fixed JabRef/Zettlr examples still support practical utility. Do not use false positives to erase the end-to-end contribution.
maintainer_evidence.feedback_effect_unknown: The final paper acknowledges developer-intended cases may affect reported TP. The exact mapping of every later maintainer response back to all table labels was not established here.

lessons_for_current_design.lesson: Separate risk discovery, legal witness construction and correctness judgment.
lessons_for_current_design.transfer: Use LLM reasoning to nominate source-bound distinction hypotheses and retrieve concrete fixtures; use execution to establish formation/reachability/same-operation fact reads; require a public behavioral contract for the final assertion.
lessons_for_current_design.why: Ripple's architecture makes the three jobs explicit, but its LLM impact prose and intent classifier do not by themselves verify executable distinctions or violations.
lessons_for_current_design.preserve: Keep source node IDs as source identity, not proof of execution or aliasing.

lessons_for_current_design.lesson: Broaden around prior responsibilities, not only the requested fix.
lessons_for_current_design.transfer: Optionally use available repository history, related tests/fixtures and public linked issues as evidence for behaviors that must be preserved. Tie each retrieved item to concrete changed source and provenance. Original validation trajectory can play a task-local role rather than constructing a huge global SKB.
lessons_for_current_design.why: Preceding change intents use old responsibilities of reused lines to expose cross-scenario side effects.
lessons_for_current_design.limit: History overlap is a prioritization clue; keep bounded lookup and time/provenance gates. Do not import hidden benchmark failure tests, gold patches or hindsight target explanations into online generation.

lessons_for_current_design.lesson: Change the triggering context before multiplying random values.
lessons_for_current_design.transfer: Consider alternate call entry points, wrappers, receiver/alias identity, setup order and ambient state in addition to boundary values. Retain the relevant operation/shared objects so the candidate tests the intended pair of facts.
lessons_for_current_design.why: Ripple distinguishes event-sequence enrichment from data enrichment. Its missed Username-sort/new-login combination shows separate feature execution can miss a joint trigger condition.
lessons_for_current_design.limit: A scenario-combination story is motivation, not evidence that the current distinction search has succeeded.

lessons_for_current_design.lesson: Be precise about where feedback acts.
lessons_for_current_design.transfer: Our proposed differentiator is runtime feedback that guides local test edits toward a particular source-bound distinction, with phases such as not reached, one fact only, both facts same operation, relation separated, and public observation.
lessons_for_current_design.why: Ripple adapts GUI execution but does not feed source coverage or a failed semantic distinction back into test generation.
lessons_for_current_design.limit: Do not claim 'execution feedback' alone is new; make the particular feedback variable, search state and observable improvement explicit.

lessons_for_current_design.lesson: A behavioral difference is a candidate observation, not a correctness oracle.
lessons_for_current_design.transfer: Keep independent public contract_refs, allow unresolved or intended behavior, and separate distinction_only from defect_revealing_augmentation. If old/new differential execution is added, use the old version as evidence rather than a universal gold oracle. Keep gold patch offline.
lessons_for_current_design.why: The detector prompt strongly labels differences outside stated intent as bugs; final §5 admits underspecified intents, beneficial unanticipated changes and necessary consequences. Maintainer responses provide concrete counterexamples.

lessons_for_current_design.lesson: Validate the instrumentation and action binding before judging the product.
lessons_for_current_design.transfer: Record actual runtime reads and operation identity, distinguish unknown/missing events, strip instrumentation and rerun a final witness. Do not infer that a planned action happened from the generated test text.
lessons_for_current_design.why: Ripple reports false positives from assumed unperformed actions and mismatched coordinates, and misses caused by incorrect execution. Those have direct analogues in fixture/setup failure and cross-invocation fact joins.

lessons_for_current_design.lesson: Evaluate the mechanism under matched budget.
lessons_for_current_design.transfer: After the current first target-binding gate, compare same-target direct generation with runtime-guided local search using the same online materials and budgets. Separately measure source-valid targets, formed inputs, reached/bound fact pairs, distinctions, public violations, gold-relative offline pass/fail, and any later repair success.
lessons_for_current_design.why: Ripple's system evidence is useful, but no ablation isolates its generation stages. The current design can answer a narrower causal question rather than merely assemble another multi-stage agent.
lessons_for_current_design.limit: This is a recommended future experiment, not an experiment run or an effectiveness claim.

concise_answer_to_parent.algorithm: diff + intent + blame-derived preceding intents → GPT-5.2 risk/scenario generation → SKB alternative-trigger enrichment → concrete-data enrichment → Claude Opus 4.5 screenshot/action loop on post-change → deterministic pre-change replay → pixel differences → GPT-5.2 intendedness classification + report filtering.
concise_answer_to_parent.program_analysis: Code-line/commit traceability and pixel processing are algorithmic; impact propagation and scenario reasoning are LLM-based. No source-level reachability, dataflow or dependency analysis is established.
concise_answer_to_parent.evidence: 111 PRs; post-filter 146 TP/173 FP reports, 45.8% precision; 117 deduplicated discoveries with caveats; known Firefox regressions 13/46; paper reporting snapshot 18 fixed + 3 confirmed + 5 intended; 54.8 min/$6 per PR; no published ablation/baseline.
concise_answer_to_parent.transferable: Use history and concrete scenario knowledge to nominate neglected contexts; preserve separation between generation, execution and oracle. Our runtime source-fact distinction is a more explicit search signal; its value still requires matched-budget evaluation. Keep gold offline.

unresolved: No actual SKB entries/retrieval logs audited, so temporal-gate discrepancy is not proof of leakage.
No complete reconciliation of final Table 1 labels with every live maintainer outcome.
No provider-run replication, benchmark execution, or runtime validation of artifact behavior performed.
No claim that all future/user-visible regressions can be detected, or that these results transfer directly to non-GUI repository issue resolution.
final_rq_answers: RQ1: An LLM-centered semantic workflow with lightweight repository traceability, text retrieval, concrete GUI execution and pixel differencing; adaptive execution exists, but execution-guided scenario search does not.

RQ2: End-to-end real-world utility is supported, with substantial report false positives and 28.3% known-bug recall in the selected Firefox set. Component effects and equal-budget advantage are not measured.

RQ3: Borrow responsibility/context diversification, retrieval-grounded trigger construction and evidence separation. Preserve the current source/runtime binding and independent public-contract oracle, and test its added value rather than infer it from Ripple.

design_reconsideration.status: Design inference for discussion, not a claim tested by RippleGUItester and not an implementation edit.
design_reconsideration.recommendation: Treat source-bound two-fact equality/identity/Boolean separation as one precise checking mechanism for suitable targets, not a universal admissibility gate for every neglected behavior.
design_reconsideration.reason: RippleGUItester exposes useful forms of hypothesis: alternative entry point, multi-step precondition, specific ambient-state combination, concrete input variation, and missing user-visible observation. These can be worth testing even when no natural pair of existing AST facts expresses the gap.
design_reconsideration.broader_target_form: Trajectory-supported neglected scenario or behavioral hypothesis + concrete trigger/setup proposal + public observation/contract + a selectable executable progress check. The progress check can be source-fact separation when applicable, or actual setup/entry/sequence/observation completion.
design_reconsideration.guardrail: Widening targets must not turn LLM scenario prose into an unverified runtime fact. Each selected progress check still needs supported execution and provenance, and gold remains offline.
design_reconsideration.evaluation: Compare coverage and utility of the two-fact subset with broader source/trajectory-grounded scenario targets before declaring the equality gate necessary. No such evaluation was run.
